2 Hoc Procli opus hodie exstare non videtur. Idem sine dubio in scholiis ad Commentarios in Rempublicam Platonis (t. II, p. 371, 18 ed. Kroll) designatur verbis: ἐν τοῖς εἰς τὴν τρίτην ἐννεάδα. Tertiae enim Enneadis Plotini capita II et III de providentia agunt.
sections.en:
1 On Demophilus, cf. Boll in Pauly-Wissowa, Realencycl., V, 147, no. 12.
2 This work of Proclus does not seem to exist today. The same is undoubtedly designated in the scholia to the Commentaries on Plato's Republic (vol. II, p. 371, 18 ed. Kroll) by the words: ἐν τοῖς εἰς τὴν τρίτην ἐννεάδα. For chapters II and III of the Third Ennead of Plotinus deal with providence.

summary.headline: Planetary Phases and Nativity Significations
summary.text: Astrological significations assigned to the planets and stellar phases: Zeus/Jupiter signifies rulers and honors, Ares/Mars soldiers and warfare, Kronos/Saturn agriculture and elders, Aphrodite/Venus marriages and artistic activities, and Hermes/Mercury speech-based professions. Demophilus’s nativity rules connect eastern phases, exaltations, pivots, settings, depressions, retrogradations, and stations with power, success, weakness, defeat, flight, wealth, and stability; Proclus relates stellar exaltations and depressions to actions and decline.
